documented_differences.name: D1: Core contract outage, Core-independent RPC
documented_differences.justification: Both gateways require an online Core session verdict per session-gated request; the Node gateway obtains it DB-to-DB (auth.sessions), the Edge gateway over HTTPS from the Core contract `session` op. With the contract endpoint down the Edge gateway has no authorized transport for the verdict and fails closed; the Node gateway keeps its DB transport. Not reproducible on the Edge gateway without DB-to-DB, a revocation window or a new Core surface.
documented_differences.counterpart: evidence/d1-session-authority.json (E2: Node refuses everything when core-db is down; E4: one verdict per Edge request, none cached)

d1_review.status: ACCEPTED — known availability trade-off, not a security regression (operator decision 2026-09-15)

decision.classification: KNOWN AVAILABILITY TRADE-OFF, NOT SECURITY REGRESSION
decision.what_was_accepted: Both gateways require an ONLINE Core session verdict for every authenticated Torneos request. The Node gateway obtained it DB-to-DB from auth.sessions; the Edge gateway obtains it over HTTPS through the Core contract (`session` op, v1.1). Preserving the Node behaviour during a core-functions outage would require violating a constraint already decided (DB-to-DB, verdict cache / revocation window, shared Core service_role, or a new authority surface on Core).
approved_remote_semantics: every authenticated Torneos request requires a CURRENT Core session verdict
never serve with a stale session
revocation / ban / soft-delete stay immediate (next request)
no DB-to-DB between Torneos and Core
decision.documented_as: known availability dependency: the availability of the Core Edge Functions runtime (torneos-core-contract) is on the per-request critical path of every session-gated Torneos request, in addition to GoTrue and the Core database that were already on the Node gateway's critical path
decision.alternatives_note: not to be implemented in Phase 3B; A/B degrade revocation, C/D/E expand trust or open a new Core surface, F does not restore equivalence

basis.note: the decision is bound to these evidence values, not to file bytes: if a re-run of d1.test.mjs changes any of them, summarize.py marks the decision stale and Phase 3B falls back to BLOCKED until it is re-confirmed

d1_review.conclusion: D1 is not a fail-closed regression: neither gateway serves a session-gated request without an online Core session verdict. The difference is the identity of the verdict transport (Node: auth.sessions DB-to-DB; Edge: Core contract `session` over HTTPS). Preserving the Node behaviour on the Edge gateway requires DB-to-DB, a revocation window, or a new Core surface / trust expansion — STOP, decision for the operator.

node_refusal_when_core_db_down.note: pre-existing mapping gap of the certified Node gateway: refusal preserved, status 401 instead of 503
